clue.text: Like a language teaching anthology that's more varied in style

indicators.note: the reworked letters are placed inside the word that follows

parts.note: chic is stylishness, elegance

indicators.note: letters that are varied are changed about, so the words before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A schoolbook of language extracts is praised for having more stylistic variety than its rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'that's' reads like a link but is part of the fodder; the stylish word is split open to hold the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A chrestomathy is an anthology of passages used for learning a language, and the adjective describes such a collection.

clue.text: Nylon component forming two types of headgear Carol's seen out in

indicators.note: the jumbled name is seen inside, between the two hats
out here means disordered, so the name is jumbled

parts.note: first type of headgear: a cap
the name, to be jumbled
second type of headgear: a tam, a Scottish bonnet

explanation.surface: Carol is spotted out wearing a nylon outfit and two hats.
explanation.walkthrough: Caprolactam is the chemical from which nylon-6 is made; the jumbled name sits between the two hats.
explanation.definitionFit: Caprolactam is the monomer polymerised to make nylon-6, so it is a building block of that synthetic fibre.

clue.text: House on meadow suggesting Gruyère?

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for house
a ley (or lea) is grassland, a meadow

explanation.surface: A farmhouse in a meadow conjures up thoughts of Swiss cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: Gruyère is popularly pictured full of holes.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of holes, as cartoon Swiss cheese is imagined to be, so a cheese like Gruyère is the image.

clue.text: Pullman sleeper? Tome judders with enveloping roar

indicators.note: the next word wraps round the shaken letters

parts.note: rote is an old word for the roar of the surf

indicators.note: something that judders shakes violently, shaking these letters about

parts.note: taken as written, to be shaken up

explanation.surface: A heavy book jolts about in a noisy train compartment.
explanation.walkthrough: Rote here is not memorising but an old word for the roar of breaking surf; it is split open around the shuffled book.
explanation.definitionFit: A roomette is a small private sleeping compartment on an American railway car, such as a Pullman.

clue.text: Suit we got altered years ago

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one of the four suits in a pack of cards
second meaning: an obsolete word for castrated people, from Latin spado

explanation.surface: We had a suit taken in some years back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Altered' is a euphemism for neutered, and 'years ago' flags that this second sense is obsolete; 'we' are the people so treated.
explanation.definitionFit: Spade is an old word for a eunuch or gelded animal, so its plural fits people who were castrated.

clue.text: Yon Scots resident in Perth, aimless

indicators.note: a resident lives inside, so the answer lives inside the following words

parts.note: found spanning the end of the city and the start of the adjective

explanation.surface: A Scotsman living in Perth drifts about without purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Thaim is a Scots form of them or those, matching the dialect pointing word yon.

clue.text: Seaman, dull and dejected

parts.note: mat (or matt) means dull, not glossy
feeling low is feeling dejected

explanation.surface: A sailor described as both boring and miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: Matlow (or matelot) is British slang for a sailor in the navy.

clue.text: Bill Mount, company man?

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
a tor is a rocky hill

explanation.surface: Bill Mount sounds like a man's name, perhaps a corporate employee.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill Mount reads as a person's name, but the two words are separate pieces; the company is a theatrical one, not a firm.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor is a member of a theatre company, so a company man in the stage sense.

clue.text: Peer, old-fashioned and also brought up after minimum of tenderness initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the smallest part of tenderness, its first letter

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing up a word makes it read from bottom to top

parts.note: too means also

explanation.surface: An aristocrat of the old school, raised with very little affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' looks like a lord, but it is the verb to look; toot is an archaic word for peep or peer.
explanation.definitionFit: Toot once meant to peep or gaze, an obsolete verb now replaced by look or peer.

clue.text: Debussy piece is about e.g. Balthazar

indicators.note: about here means around, so the first word wraps the second

parts.note: taken as written
Balthazar was one of the Magi, the wise men; one is a mage

explanation.surface: A Debussy composition is said to be about one of the Three Kings.
explanation.definitionFit: Images is the title of two sets of piano pieces and an orchestral work by Debussy.

clue.text: Time short, enter carelessly in monthly AZ affairs — hitch resulting

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the competitions

parts.note: Azed runs a monthly clue-writing competition, the comps

indicators.note: done carelessly, the letters land any old how

parts.note: T is the short form of time
taken as written, to be jumbled

explanation.surface: Short of time, a competitor sends in a careless entry to the monthly Azed contest and things go wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: AZ is Azed himself, whose monthly clue-writing competitions are known as comps.
explanation.definitionFit: A contretemps is an unexpected mishap or embarrassing snag, so a hitch.

clue.text: Reverse of high pressure — low: that's it

indicators.note: reverse of asks for the following letters read backwards

parts.note: HP is the abbreviation for high pressure
to low is to moo, as cattle do

explanation.surface: A weather note: the opposite of a high is a low, and that's that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like the weather system, but it is the cow's call; 'it' is the old slang for sex appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Oomph means vigour or sex appeal, which old slang also called 'it', as in the It girl.

clue.text: Dressmaker's marker is flattering with depth of colour

parts.note: to soap someone is to flatter them, so one who is flattering soaps
tone is the shade or depth of a colour

explanation.surface: A tailor's chalk mark is praised for its rich colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' belongs with 'flattering' to make a verb form: he soaps, he is flattering.
explanation.definitionFit: Soapstone, or French chalk, is the soft mineral tailors use to mark cloth before cutting.

clue.text: Trot e.g. in Perth as usual cut short

indicators.note: cutting a word short means removing its last letter

parts.note: common means usual, ordinary

explanation.surface: Someone trotting in Perth, Scotland, as normal but briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: This time Perth is in Western Australia, not Scotland; a Trot is a Trotskyist, and commo is Australian slang for a communist.
explanation.definitionFit: Commo is Australian slang for a communist, and a Trotskyist is an example of one.

clue.text: Old steersman, one having bailed out, showing pluck

indicators.note: bailing out is leaving the aircraft, so that piece leaves the word

parts.note: pilot in its old sense of a helmsman
I is the Roman numeral one, to be removed

explanation.surface: A former pilot shows courage by parachuting out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pluck' looks like courage, which suits the pilot story; it is the verb, to strip a bird of feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: Plot is a Scots verb meaning to scald and pluck a fowl, so it matches pluck as a verb.

clue.text: Corded silk from wildly excessive sultanate

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means wildly excessive
Oman is a sultanate on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: Luxurious ribbed silk sourced from an extravagant Gulf state.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottoman is a heavy ribbed fabric of silk or wool, named after the Turkish empire.

clue.text: Curative skin lotion (not the first) applied to face

indicators.note: not the first means dropping the opening letter

parts.note: a crème is a cream or lotion
dial is slang for a face, and a clock face is its dial

explanation.surface: A healing lotion is rubbed on the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Remedial means intended to cure or put right, so it is a synonym of curative.

clue.text: A lass bursting with ire, aggressive one

indicators.note: bursting breaks the letters apart so they can be put back in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl boiling over with anger turns violent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' joins the two lots of fodder; both must be mixed together.
explanation.definitionFit: An assailer is one who attacks, so an aggressor or aggressive person.

clue.text: One deliberately delays fiddling with spirometer

indicators.note: fiddling with something messes it about, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a lung-capacity gauge, taken as written

explanation.surface: A patient stalls for time by toying with the breathing test device.
explanation.definitionFit: A temporiser plays for time, stalling to avoid committing to a decision.

clue.text: News just breaking from Louisiana trial

parts.note: LA is the postal abbreviation for Louisiana
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: Breaking news from a court case in Louisiana.
explanation.definitionFit: The latest is the most recent news, as in 'have you heard the latest?'

clue.text: Head off sharp pain during a quinsy, say

indicators.note: with its head off, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a pang is a sudden sharp pain
in means during, as in 'in the night'
taken as written

explanation.surface: A stabbing pain strikes while suffering from a sore throat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'During' looks like a link but supplies letters; angina in its older sense is any inflammation of the throat, of which quinsy is one.
explanation.definitionFit: Angina once meant any throat inflammation, and quinsy, an abscess near the tonsils, is an example.

clue.text: Poet's single? Tense one comparable to Monty D, perhaps

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

parts.words: one comparable to Monty D, perhaps
parts.note: Alan T(itchmarsh), a TV gardener like Monty Don

explanation.surface: A nervous poet's solo, likened to a celebrity gardener's.
explanation.walkthrough: Monty Don and Alan Titchmarsh are both well-known British TV gardening presenters. Talant is Milton's spelling of talon; the question mark makes 'single' a single claw.
explanation.definitionFit: Talant is an old poetic spelling of talon, and a single talon is one claw.

clue.text: What's in German river, tail moving a lot? Bony fish

indicators.note: the final letter travels a long way toward the front of the word

parts.note: a river holds water, which in German is Wasser

explanation.surface: A fish in a German river, wagging its tail vigorously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's in German' tempts you to WAS; the phrase means what a river contains, in German. Its last letter moves up to second place.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrasses are spiny-finned sea fishes with bony skeletons, as opposed to cartilaginous sharks and rays.

clue.text: Hatred in mess for staff officer (6, two words)

indicators.note: letters in a mess are disordered, needing to be sorted into a new word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Loathing in the officers' mess for a staff officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mess' looks like the officers' dining room, which suits the military surface, but it signals disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: Red hat is British army slang for a staff officer, from the red band on their caps.

clue.text: A chinwag about ayurveda or what's complementary to terres-trial stuff?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about means around, so the chat goes round the medicine

parts.note: a natter is a chat
Ayurveda is traditional Indian medicine, abbreviated TIM

explanation.surface: A chat about alternative medicine, which some see as complementary to earthbound science.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complementary' plays on complementary medicine; the definition is physics. Ayurveda is traditional Indian medicine, TIM for short.
explanation.definitionFit: Antimatter is made of antiparticles, the counterpart to the ordinary matter found on Earth.

clue.text: Minuscule portions helping to make hermit esurient

indicators.note: the answer helps make up the next words, sitting within them

parts.note: found spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Tiny helpings are enough to make a recluse ravenous.
explanation.walkthrough: Esurient means hungry.
explanation.definitionFit: A mite is a very small amount or portion, as in the widow's mite.

clue.text: Hole, last for rabbit in quitting former abode

indicators.note: last for points to the final letter of the following word

parts.note: the final letter of rabbit

indicators.note: quitting means leaving, so those letters leave the word

parts.note: remain is an obsolete noun meaning abode
taken as written, to be removed

explanation.surface: A rabbit's burrow is the last thing left on leaving its old home.
explanation.walkthrough: Remain was once a noun meaning a dwelling or stay; dropping its IN leaves REMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A trema is an anatomical orifice or perforation, from the Greek word for hole.

clue.text: Ponting's boast: Australia's third outfit's superior to England's first

indicators.note: third points to the third letter of the preceding word

parts.note: the third letter of Australia
kit is an outfit; the 's means is

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the preceding word

parts.note: the first letter of England

explanation.surface: The Australian cricket captain brags that his team's kit beats England's.
explanation.walkthrough: Ricky Ponting captained Australia at cricket; skite is Australian slang for boasting. In a down clue 'superior to' means placed above.
explanation.definitionFit: Skite is Australian and New Zealand slang for a boast or to brag, fitting an Australian speaker.

clue.text: Berate falling off in careful food shop

indicators.note: the first word falls away from the word it sits in

parts.note: deliberate means careful and unhurried
taken as written, to be removed

explanation.surface: Tell someone off for slipping over in a fussy grocer's.
explanation.definitionFit: Deli is short for delicatessen, a shop selling prepared foods.

clue.text: Killed foully after imbibing tincture — reminiscent of Lucan?

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the scrambled word takes the other inside
done foully means messed up, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, to be scrambled
or is the heraldic tincture gold

explanation.surface: A murder committed after drinking, which brings Lord Lucan to mind.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Lucan vanished in 1974 after his children's nanny was murdered, hence the grim surface; the definition only needs him to be a lord.
explanation.definitionFit: Lordlike means befitting a lord, and Lucan was a peer, Lord Lucan.

clue.text: Badly bitten, one admitted describing misnamed terrier?

indicators.note: something admitted is let inside the other letters
badly arranged letters need putting into a different order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a means one

explanation.surface: Someone badly bitten by a dog wrongly called a terrier.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tibetan terrier is not a true terrier but a herding and companion dog, hence 'misnamed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tibetan is the adjective in the breed name Tibetan terrier, a dog not genuinely of the terrier group.

clue.text: Swell drooping when rear moves to front

indicators.note: the final letter is taken from the back and put at the start

parts.note: limp means drooping

explanation.surface: Something swollen sags when its back end shifts forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Plim is a dialect verb meaning to swell or fill out.

clue.text: Imbecile, kind of cuckoo, with extremes of lassitude

indicators.note: extremes are the two ends, the first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of lassitude

explanation.surface: A fool, a bit cuckoo and utterly listless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuckoo' tempts as the definition of crazy; it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Anile means like a feeble old woman, so doting or imbecile in the old sense of weak-minded.

clue.text: Pre-Impressionist stays on

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the French painter who preceded the Impressionists
second meaning: Latin for 'he or she remains', a stage direction

explanation.surface: An early painter remains in place.
explanation.walkthrough: Manet is the Latin stage direction that a character remains on stage, the opposite of exit.
explanation.definitionFit: Édouard Manet's painting led the way to Impressionism, and manet in a script means one actor remains.

clue.text: One needs ages to circumvent a main point with rule in law offices

indicators.note: to circumvent is to go round, so the ageing word surrounds the rest

parts.note: one who ages matures
taken as written
the gist is the main point
R is short for rule

explanation.surface: Someone needs years to get round a main point of law in legal chambers.
explanation.walkthrough: The surrounding verb is split after its first letter to take in A, GIST and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A magistrature is the office or dignity of a magistrate, so the plural names such posts.
